test oracle.note: Many Norwegian testers keep 'oracle' in English.

automation bias.note: Many Norwegian testers keep 'automation bias' in English — newer term from CT-AI v1.0, post-dates the NO glossary.

accessibility.note: 'Universell utforming' is the Norwegian legal term (Likestillings- og diskrimineringsloven §17).

scenarios.label: Test scenarios from a requirement / user story

anchors.summary: Derive test cases from specifications using equivalence partitioning (§4.2.1), boundary value analysis (§4.2.2), decision tables (§4.2.3) and state transition (§4.2.4).
Prioritise derived cases by risk, change frequency, complexity and coverage — not alphabetically or by order of writing.

anchors.section: §11.3 Using AI for Test Case Generation
anchors.summary: LLMs can generate test cases from requirements, but the oracle problem remains: a human must validate expected results.
Risk = likelihood × impact, split into project risks and product risks; drives test effort allocation.
Identify, assess and rank product risks so testing depth is proportional to exposure — not treated uniformly.
Shift heavy coverage to lower, cheaper levels (unit) while reserving expensive E2E effort for the highest-risk flows.

ambiguities.label: Hidden assumptions & ambiguous terms in a user story

anchors.summary: Ambiguity is a defect detectable without execution — static testing finds it before it reaches code.
Stories should be Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable (INVEST) — ambiguity violates Testable.
Acceptance criteria must be unambiguous and verifiable; missing or vague criteria are the primary ambiguity signal.
Concurrent test design, execution and learning; uses tester experience, intuition and heuristics. Best structured via session-based test management (charters, time-boxed).
For AI/ML systems, exploratory testing plus exploratory data analysis (EDA) is often the only feasible approach where the oracle is weak.

followups.label: Follow-up questions for a thin / vague bug report

anchors.summary: A defect report's core content must include preconditions, steps, expected vs actual, environment, severity — follow-ups fill the gaps so the report is reproducible.
Treat a bug report like a review artefact: questions should surface missing context, not debate the fix.

anchors.section: §11.2 Using AI to Analyze Reported Defects
anchors.summary: AI can cluster and triage defects at scale, but extracting reproduction steps from a vague report still benefits from human follow-up.

automation.label: Test automation code from a requirement

anchors.section: §6.2 Benefits and Risks of Test Automation
anchors.summary: Automation scales repeatable checks and frees humans for exploratory/risk work — but flaky tests and maintenance cost can eclipse the benefit.
Automate heavy at unit level, thin at E2E; inverted pyramids are an anti-pattern that produces slow, brittle suites.
Good automation code follows the same engineering principles as production code: layering (test adaption / definition / execution), independence, deterministic data.

testData.label: Test data generation for a feature

anchors.summary: Data should cover each equivalence class at least once — both valid and invalid partitions.
Values at and around boundaries are disproportionately likely to expose defects.
For AI/ML testing, dataset quality (representativeness, balance, labelling accuracy) drives test validity more than volume.

anchors.section: §7.3 Test Data for Testing AI-Based Systems
anchors.summary: Distinguish training, validation, and test datasets — never let test data leak into training.
For probabilistic AI systems a perfect oracle rarely exists; use surrogate oracles (pseudo-oracles, statistical oracles, human oracles, consistency oracles).
When direct ground truth is unavailable, use metamorphic relations: 'if I transform the input in way X, the output should change in way Y'.
Compare two implementations (or the same implementation on equivalent inputs) to detect discrepancies without needing a golden oracle.
Triage classifies defects by severity (technical impact) and priority (business urgency) — the two are independent dimensions.
Triage is risk reasoning applied to a single defect: likelihood of reoccurrence × impact on user/business.
Track aggregate triage signals (defect age, reopened rate, severity distribution) — not just counts.
Heuristic/checklist testing is the canonical ISTQB approach for accessibility and usability — WCAG and Nielsen heuristics are the de-facto checklists.
Accessibility testing combines automated scanners (axe, Lighthouse) with manual checks — automation finds ~30–40% of WCAG issues.

external_standards.note: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2, success criteria at levels A / AA / AAA.
EU accessibility standard; Norway's 'Likestillings- og diskrimineringsloven §17' references it.
10 usability heuristics — 'visibility of system status', 'error prevention', etc.

router.label: Routing a free-text problem to the correct testing round

anchors.summary: Choosing the right technique is itself a taught skill: black-box for requirements-driven, white-box for code-driven, experience-based when spec is weak.
When multiple techniques could apply, prioritise by risk exposure and business value, not by convenience.

judge.label: Judging the quality of a human vs AI testing answer

anchors.summary: Test quality is multi-dimensional (coverage, defect detection effectiveness, traceability) — a long answer that misses the oracle is not a better answer.
For AI-assisted testing, the right yardstick is whether the answer advances the stated test objective — not stylistic polish.
